name: Non-academic Problem
description: You are given a connected undirected graph, the vertices of which are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Your task is to minimize the number of pairs of vertices $$$1 \leq u \lt v \leq n$$$ between which there exists a path in this graph. To achieve this, you can remove exactly one edge from the graph. Find the smallest number of pairs of vertices!
input_specification: Each test consists of several sets of input data. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of sets of input data. Then follows their description. The first line of each set of input data contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$, $$$n - 1 \leq m \leq \min(10^5, \frac{n \cdot (n - 1)}{2})$$$) — the number of vertices in the graph and the number of edges. Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq u, v \leq n, u \neq v$$$), indicating that there is an undirected edge in the graph between vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given graph is connected and without multiple edges. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ and the sum of $$$m$$$ over all sets of input data does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each set of input data, output the smallest number of pairs of reachable vertices, if exactly one edge can be removed.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1986F — Non-academic Problem [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
